title: Page-aware KV slot coalescing and prefetch policy for paged-attention
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Reduce KV cache fragmentation and unnecessary evictions in the paged-attention design while improving prefill/decode tail latency by coordinating kernel selection, page prefetching, and slot coalescing. This ticket introduces a page-aware KV slot coalescer and adaptive prefetch policy that work together with kernel routing hints to minimize redundant memory churn and warm up kernels for imminent decodes.

Context: Our paged attention layout stores KV entries in fixed-size page slots on GPU memory. Fragmentation and small sparse allocations lead to frequent compaction and eviction storms during high-concurrency workloads. Current prefill logic issues blind page fetches which sometimes trigger eviction of hot slots and cause extra kernel reinitialization. This increases token tail latency and increases GPU memory bandwidth.

Proposal summary:
- Introduce a slot coalescer that merges adjacent underutilized slots on a per-page basis when occupancy falls below a tunable threshold, reducing fragmentation and total allocated page count.
- Implement an eviction scoring function that combines recency, per-token hit-rate (hotness), and "kernel affinity" (a hint tied to the model variant / quantization profile) so the eviction policy favors removing slots that hurt kernel reuse the least.
- Add an adaptive prefetch policy that: (1) prioritizes prefetching pages for short upcoming decode spans; (2) staggers prefetches when system-wide eviction pressure is high; (3) issues kernel warmup commands (lightweight warms) for the selected model-kernel pair so planned decodes avoid cold-kernel latencies.
- Expose two knobs in runtime config: slot_coalesce_threshold (0-1 occupancy) and prefetch_aggressiveness (0-3). Both default to conservative values for backwards-compatibility.
acceptance_criteria: Reduce measured KV page fragmentation index by >= 30% on mixed-concurrency chat benchmark compared to baseline (no coalescing)
Decrease 99th percentile token latency during prefill+decode by >= 20% on 8xA10 mixed workload with active autoscaling OFF
Eviction churn (pages evicted per minute) reduced by >= 25% at 80% memory utilization
Feature gated rollout with runtime flag and telemetry showing kernel-warmup hit-rate > 70% for prefetched workloads
Unit tests for slot coalescer, eviction scorer, and prefetch scheduling; end-to-end bench harness reproducing metrics
implementation_plan: Design: finalize slot data-structure changes and locking semantics (1 week)
Runtime: implement slot coalescer module that runs as low-priority background compactor with backoff and scoped mutexes (2 weeks)
Eviction: add weighted eviction scorer using (recency, hit-rate, kernel-affinity) and integrate with existing reclaim path (1 week)
Prefetch: implement adaptive scheduler that reads per-route decode distributions and issues page fetch + kernel warmup commands (2 weeks)
Testing: add microbenchmarks (fragmentation, eviction churn), integration harness (prefill/decode tail), and chaos tests for concurrent prefetch+evict (1 week)
Rollout: feature flag behind runtime.prefill.coalesce with canary on <5% traffic, monitor metrics, then gradual ramp (2 weeks)
tradeoffs: Background coalescing uses GPU cycles and adds complexity to allocator paths; we limit work to low-priority epochs to avoid affecting foreground latency
Kernel affinity heuristics require tracking extra metadata per slot and may bias eviction in unexpected ways for rarely-used kernels; we will log metrics to detect negative regressions
Prefetch aggressiveness increases memory pressure; conservative defaults and backoff prevent runaway thrashing but may under-prefetch in some tail cases
comments: 2025-01-10 - Asha Kapoor: Initial write-up and rationale. Attached rough microbenchmark results showing fragmentation index = 0.42 baseline on mixed-chat. Starting design review.
2025-01-14 - Marco D'Souza (PM): Suggested adding a kernel-affinity metric to the eviction scorer to preserve warm kernels used by Dedicated customers. Asked for per-tenant telemetry filters.

2025-01-20 - Jin Park (Staff Engine): Reviewed compaction locking plan. Requested we avoid global allocator pauses; recommended epoch-based sharded coalescer. Action: update design to shard by page-range.

2025-01-25 - Design Review: Agreed to provide a conservative default for slot_coalesce_threshold=0.25 and prefetch_aggressiveness=1. Marco to coordinate product notes for Dedicated customers. Asha to implement prototype.

2025-01-30 - Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2198 - prototype coalescer + eviction scorer. Benchmark in PR shows initial token_p99 improvement ~12% on 4-concurrent streams. Needs more stress tests.

2025-02-02 - Load test: Canary run on staging with 50% mem util shows eviction churn down 28% and prefetched kernel warmup hit-rate 64%. Observed an edge-case where coalescing increased page remapping latency for very small ephemeral contexts (ticketed to follow-up).
Next steps: finalize PR with sharded coalescer, add chaos tests that simulate bursts, and prepare canary rollout plan with SLO guards.
